title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space and defense sectors are buzzing with contract wins and new technology developments. Notably, NASA's lunar mission successor has been selected, while the upper C-band auction continues to bolster the GEO industry.

themes.title: NASA's Lunar Ambitions
themes.body: NASA's recent selection for the CAPSTONE successor signals a renewed focus on lunar exploration. This move could set the stage for more ambitious missions and partnerships in the coming years.

themes.title: GEO Industry Gains Traction
themes.body: The upper C-band auction is proving to be a financial boon for the GEO sector, with SES poised to reap significant rewards. This trend underscores the growing importance of spectrum management in satellite operations.

themes.title: Defense Contracts on the Rise
themes.body: Sphinx Defense's $287 million contract for satellite communications software highlights a robust demand for secure military communications. As geopolitical tensions rise, expect more such contracts to emerge.

themes.title: Tech Innovations in Space
themes.body: Intel's new chip for space computing and Orbes' Exo-ORB unveilings reflect the ongoing tech race in the space sector. These advancements are crucial for enhancing operational capabilities in increasingly complex missions.
